<explanation>
1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a full-stack, containerized, microservice-based security framework (“RedAmon”) that automates offensive security operations end-to-end: reconnaissance, graph storage, AI-driven exploitation, post-exploitation, and a Next.js web UI.  
   - It uses Docker Compose to orchestrate multiple services (frontend, backends, tool servers, databases, test targets) communicating via well-defined APIs, WebSockets, REST/SSE, and the Model Context Protocol.

2. Analyze the File Structure  
   - Top-level folders and services:  
     • webapp (Next.js UI, Prisma ORM, PostgreSQL)  
     • agentic (AI Orchestrator, FastAPI + LangGraph + WebSocket API)  
     • recon_orchestrator (FastAPI + Docker SDK for scanning pipeline)  
     • recon (Kali-based Python recon pipeline)  
     • mcp (Kali sandbox tool servers: Naabu, Curl, Nuclei, Metasploit)  
     • graph_db (Neo4j client & schema)  
     • gvm_scan (Greenbone Vulnerability Manager scanner)  
     • postgres_db (PostgreSQL for project settings)  
     • guinea_pigs (vulnerable target containers)  
   - Configuration: multiple docker-compose.yml files for production, development, and per-component orchestration.

3. Examine the README for Insights  
   - High-level architecture is separated into layers: User → Frontend (Next.js) → Backend orchestrators → MCP tool servers → Data stores → Targets.  
   - Detailed sequence diagrams, Mermaid flows, and ER diagrams describe data flow and component interactions.

4. Main Components & Their Relationships  
   a. Components  
      - User Layer: Browser UI / CLI  
      - Frontend Layer: Next.js webapp container (:3000)  
      - Backend Layer:  
        • AI Agent Orchestrator (FastAPI + LangGraph, WebSocket API :8090)  
        • Recon Orchestrator (FastAPI, Docker SDK :8010)  
      - MCP Tool Layer: Naabu Server (:8000), Curl Server (:8001), Nuclei Server (:8002), Metasploit Server (:8003)  
      - Recon Pipeline Container: six-phase Kali-based Python scanner (crt.sh, Naabu, Httpx, Katana, Nuclei, MITRE enrichment)  
      - Data Layer: Neo4j graph database (:7474/7687), PostgreSQL (+Prisma ORM :5432)  
      - Test Targets: Guinea Pigs (Apache containers), external target systems  
   b. Interactions  
      - Browser ↔ Webapp via HTTP(S) & WebSocket (AI chat)  
      - Webapp → Recon Orchestrator via REST + SSE (start/monitor pipeline)  
      - Recon Orchestrator → Recon Container via Docker SDK  
      - Recon Container → Neo4j (ingest graph)  
      - Webapp ↔ Neo4j (visualization, GraphQL/Cypher)  
      - Webapp ↔ PostgreSQL (project settings)  
      - Webapp ↔ Agent Orchestrator via WebSocket for steer/approve  
      - Agent → Neo4j (read for intelligence, write Exploit nodes)  
      - Agent → MCP servers via JSON-RPC SSE (invoke Naabu/Curl/Nuclei/Metasploit)  
      - MCP servers → Target or Guinea Pigs (execute scans/exploits)  
   c. Architectural Patterns  
      - Layered architecture: presentation, orchestration, tool execution, data persistence  
      - Microservices: each logical unit in its own container with isolated API  
      - Event-driven and streaming: WebSockets for real-time agent updates; SSE for logs  
      - ReAct pattern in AI agent: reasoning → tool selection → execution → observation loop  
      - Knowledge graph center: Neo4j as single source of truth  
   d. Key Technologies  
      - Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Prisma Client  
      - Backend: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph (Claude/OpenAI), Docker SDK, SSE  
      - Containerization: Docker Compose, Kali Linux sandbox  
      - Databases: Neo4j (Bolt/HTTP), PostgreSQL (Prisma ORM)  
      - Security Tools: Naabu, Httpx, Knockpy, Katana, GAU, Kiterunner, Nuclei, Metasploit, (GVM)  
      - Communication Protocols: REST, SSE, WebSocket, JSON-RPC over SSE  

5. Guidelines to Draw the System Design Diagram  
   - Define Layers as Swimlanes or Colored Zones:  
     [User Layer] → [Frontend Layer] → [Backend Layer] → [Tool Layer] → [Data Layer] → [Target Layer]  
   - Draw Container Boundaries: group related services (e.g., all MCP servers in a “Kali-MCP Sandbox” box).  
   - Show Communication Channels with Directional Arrows and Protocol Labels:  
     • HTTP / WebSocket / REST / SSE between services  
     • Docker SDK calls, JSON-RPC SSE flows  
   - Highlight Data Stores and Flows: arrows from recon pipeline into Neo4j; from webapp into PostgreSQL; from agent into Neo4j.  
   - Represent the AI Agent Loop: a sub-diagram or inset showing the ReAct cycle (reason → select tool → execute → observe).  
   - Use Color Coding or Shapes:  
     • Blue boxes for user and frontend  
     • Orange for orchestration backends  
     • Red for tool servers  
     • Purple cylinders for databases  
     • Green for target/test environments  
   - Label Each Component Clearly with Name, Technology, Port (optional)  
   - Include a Legend Explaining Colors, Shapes, and Arrow Styles  

6. Tailoring Tips for a Full-Stack, Containerized Microservice Application  
   - Emphasize strict separation of concerns: UI vs. orchestrators vs. tool servers vs. data stores  
   - Show how services scale or can be swapped (e.g., dev vs. prod webapp via compose profiles)  
   - Illustrate both synchronous (HTTP, WebSocket) and asynchronous/streaming (SSE, Docker events) interactions  
   - Capture how each stage of the recon pipeline feeds data into the graph, which the AI agent then consumes  

7. Essential Diagram Elements Checklist  
   - Clear, consistent naming for each box (component)  
   - Directional arrows for all API calls, data flows, and tool invocations  
   - Color coding and/or distinct shapes to differentiate layers  
   - Protocol annotations (e.g., WebSocket, JSON-RPC, Bolt)  
   - A legend with color/shape mapping and arrow styles  
   - (Optional) Sequence or inset sub-diagrams for complex workflows (e.g., six-phase recon, ReAct loop)  

By following these guidelines, you will produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that reflects RedAmon’s layered, containerized architecture, its microservice interactions, data flow pipelines, and the orchestration patterns that tie reconnaissance, AI reasoning, exploitation, and visualization together.
</explanation>
